base_contract: Keep the existing renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) fast path unchanged on filesystems that support it.
Enter the compatibility path only after the no-replace operation reports a positively identified unsupported-filesystem condition.
Propagate permission, I/O, quota, path, corruption, and all other non-capability errors without fallback.
Create staging content on the destination filesystem so publication cannot become a cross-device copy.
Write every checkpoint payload and metadata file completely before publication begins.
Flush and fsync every checkpoint file before publication begins.
Fsync the completed staging directory before publication begins.
Never remove, truncate, merge with, or otherwise modify a pre-existing destination.
Resolve concurrent writers with exactly one successful publisher and fail all losers closed.
Never expose a partially populated directory at the final destination name.
Do not report success until the final destination is durably published.
Fsync the destination parent directory wherever the filesystem exposes a supported directory-fsync operation.
Treat an unsupported directory fsync separately from publication failure and record the exact observed behavior.
Clean the caller's staging path after confirmed success and after every recoverable pre-publication failure.
Do not delete an ambiguous final destination after a transport error or lost acknowledgement.
Keep checkpoint bytes, metadata, schema versions, and checksums identical across publication backends.
Keep restart, tamper rejection, legacy-checkpoint loading, and cross-device identity behavior unchanged.
Cover success, collision, crash boundary, permission failure, I/O failure, and concurrency behavior with deterministic tests.
supplemental_contract: Use atomic mkdir as the compatibility-path name claim, then rename over only the empty placeholder created by that publisher.
For a non-idempotent retransmission after a possibly successful publish, read the published checkpoint back and verify it; if success cannot be confirmed, fail closed.
Measure and persist the actual NFS directory-fsync behavior on the target cluster.
Do not serialize the selected publication backend or fallback marker into checkpoint content.
Require byte-for-byte identical checkpoint trees from the fast path and compatibility path for identical input state.
Identify unsupported operation using both errno and statfs filesystem evidence, including the raw syscall(316) renameat2 path.
Run a cross-client concurrency test against the same NFS destination.
Require provider identity digests to remain unchanged.

qualification.h100: one small checkpoint/restart job only after separate user authorization
